references.text: The people said, 'Let us not be scattered over the whole earth' – exactly what the Lord brings about in v.8 as a direct consequence of their rebellion.
A summary of the Babel event: The Lord confused their language and scattered them from there over the whole earth – a direct parallel and repetition of v.8.
The name Peleg means 'division', and this verse refers to a time when the earth (or humanity) was 'divided', which can be seen as a parallel to the scattering of mankind in Gen 11:8.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance and separated the children of men from one another – a thematic parallel to the Lord's scattering of the peoples from Babel.
In Acts 2:5-11, the disciples speak in many languages so that people from all nations understand them. This can be seen as a reversal of the language confusion and scattering at Babel in Gen 11:8.
Isaiah 24:1 generalizes the principle of judgment from the Babel event to a universal eschatological judgment.
